residency.test: Resident if your main home or the seat of your wealth is in Belgium. Entry in the national register creates a rebuttable presumption of residence.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes for residents, with exemption-with-progression for treaty-exempt foreign income.
residency.expat_regime: The special tax regime for inbound taxpayers (BIRTI) allows up to 30% of gross remuneration, capped at 90,000, to be paid free of tax and social security as a cost proper to the employer.

headline.rates: 25% / 40% / 45% / 50% - the top rate starts unusually low

standard_deduction.name: Forfait de frais professionnels
standard_deduction.note: flat professional expense deduction; actual expenses may be claimed instead

personal_allowance.name: Quotité exemptée d'impôt
personal_allowance.note: the child supplement rises steeply for the second, third and later children

surcharges.name: Additionnels communaux
surcharges.note: municipal surcharge on income tax; 0% in a few municipalities, up to about 9% elsewhere

employer.name: ONSS/RSZ employer contribution
employer.note: about 25% for white-collar workers after structural reductions

self_employed.name: Cotisations sociales indépendants
self_employed.note: 20.5% up to about 76,000, then 14.16% to the ceiling

capital_gains.general: Belgium historically did not tax private capital gains realised in the normal management of private wealth. A general capital gains tax of 10% on financial assets has been agreed politically - confirm whether it is in force for the year in question.
capital_gains.speculative: gains outside normal management of private wealth are taxed at 33%
capital_gains.real_estate: 16.5% on sales of non-primary property within five years
capital_gains.dividends_interest: 30% withholding, with a partial exemption for the first tranche of dividends

quirks: The 50% bracket starts below 50,000 of taxable income, so Belgium reaches its top marginal rate at a lower income than almost any other developed country.
Social security has no ceiling, which keeps the marginal wedge high all the way up the income scale.
The municipal surcharge is applied to your tax, not your income, and depends on where you were registered on 1 January.
Company cars, meal vouchers and group insurance are heavily used precisely because cash salary is taxed so hard - the benefits package matters more than the headline salary.
Married and legally cohabiting couples file jointly and the marital quotient can transfer part of one spouse's income to the other where incomes are unequal.

reporting.who_must_file: Every resident taxpayer receives a return. Many receive a simplified proposed assessment which becomes final unless corrected.

deadlines.what: Extended online deadline for returns including self-employment or foreign income

forms.name: Personal income tax return, Parts 1 and 2

documents_to_collect: National register number and itsme or eID card reader for portal access
Mortgage certificate and life insurance statements
Details of foreign accounts, which must be reported to the National Bank as well as on the return, and of foreign property

penalties.late_filing: 50 to 1,250 administrative fine, plus an ex officio assessment
penalties.understatement: 10% to 200% tax increase depending on intent and repetition
penalties.late_payment: interest at the statutory rate, currently around 4% to 8% a year

warnings: The municipal surcharge is set to a typical 7.5%. Substitute the actual rate of the commune of residence on 1 January.
The marital quotient and the detailed child allowance scale are not modelled.
The BIRTI inbound regime is not applied; if it is available, reduce gross salary by the exempt portion before calculating.
